title: No big stars, payroll and one-nighters
summary: Greene says ensembles now outweigh soloists, and concerts, schools and festivals keep the band working.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Do you think to some extent though, that Basie over the years has learned to be a little, perhaps, distrustful of prima donnas? That he might not want to have too many big stars (laugh) to give him a headache?
I don't know. I don't know how to -- whether --
You must have had enough experience on it.
Yeah. I don't know whether that is true, or not. Or how he feels about it, you know. His reason for not having big name -- big stars.
The payroll must be a very serious factor at all times today, mustn't it? I mean, how you pay this transportation -- you've got one-nighters, and will that pay off?
Well, I don't know too much about that part of it, Stan. You know, I really don't understand what goes on, you know, as far as the payroll is concerned.
But, you know, for years now all the big bands have been doing one-nighters.
Well, we know that that's very expensive to do, because of transportation.

Well, we do alot of concerts now, you see? We're doing alot of concerts, plus, you know, like, high schools, and colleges, you know, and alot of festivals. And, I think that kind of keeps things going.
